articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the Over-the-Rectus Extrapelvic (OREX) approach defines safe zones for W-plate fixation of the anterior pelvic ring.
articles.authors: Da Cunha Q, Hellwinkel JE, Mauffrey C, David G
articles.population: Fresh-frozen adult cadavers
articles.outcomes: Identification of three anatomical layers in the pre-symphyseal region, location of critical neurovascular structures relative to pubic midline and tubercles, dimensions of ligamentous-aponeurotic complex, soft-tissue thickness, sex-related differences, and safe zones for W-plate fixation
articles.take_home: Surgeons performing W-plate fixation for pelvic fractures have predictable safe zones for placing implants in the pre-symphyseal region, with critical nerves and blood vessels located about 3.2 cm from the midline and the central area being free of these structures. The study provides specific anatomical measurements to help surgeons avoid damaging important structures during this procedure.

articles.title: Risk factors for complications following surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kojima KE, Argotte PLP, Esteves DS, Guimaraes MGV, Medina R, Abe Puccetti VLY, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent surgical fixation of pelvic ring fractures
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including surgical site infection and chronic pain
articles.take_home: About one in three patients had complications after pelvic fracture surgery, with infection occurring in roughly one in six. Having a Morel-Lavallee lesion (a soft tissue injury) or certain fracture patterns significantly increased the risk of infection after surgery.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of locking intramedullary nails versus locking plates for displaced proximal humeral fractures : a meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Alshayban MA, Mourad MA, Alasiri A, Alazzam AY, Alzahrani A
articles.study_type: Meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults with displaced proximal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (DASH score, Constant-Murley Score, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score) at early (3 months), mid-term and long-term (≥24 months) follow-up; complication rates and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Locking intramedullary nails and locking plates performed similarly for most proximal humeral fractures, but locking plates showed better results for the most complex fractures (three- and four-part fractures) and had fewer reoperations needed.

articles.title: Aspirin is safe and effective for prevention of deep vein thrombosis following acetabular fracture surgery.
articles.authors: Dinesh A, Poursalehian M, Billow D, Peirish RW, Cereijo C, Padubidri A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using real-world electronic health records and claims data
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over who underwent surgical treatment for acetabular fractures between January 2014 and December 2025
articles.sample_size: 1174 patients per cohort after propensity score matching (aspirin group and other anticoagulant group)
articles.outcomes: Deep vein thrombosis at 14, 30 and 90 days; emergency department visits, deep infection, stroke and readmission rates at 14, 30 and 90 days
articles.take_home: Aspirin was associated with lower rates of deep vein thrombosis compared to other anticoagulants at 14, 30 and 90 days after acetabular fracture surgery, with no significant differences in serious complications like infection or stroke. Aspirin may be a safe and effective alternative to traditional anticoagulants for preventing blood clots in this patient group.

articles.title: Common acetabular fracture patterns in patients with femoroacetabular impingement.
articles.authors: Garlapaty AR, Townsley S, Touhey DC, Walz JW, Duren D, Cook JL, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18-55 years treated for acetabular fracture, hip dislocation, or femoral head fracture
articles.outcomes: Acetabular fracture patterns classified by Judet and Letournel systems; complication rates
articles.take_home: Most acetabular fracture patients (72%) had femoroacetabular impingement, and whilst posterior wall fractures were most common in both groups, men with impingement were significantly more likely to have transverse fractures. The complication rate was similar between those with and without impingement (21.4% versus 27%).

articles.title: Robotic navigation-assisted versus conventional freehand placement of the infra-acetabular screw in acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Cao W, Chen Z, Liu H, Zhan N, He J, Qi L, et al.
articles.population: Patients with acetabular fractures requiring infra-acetabular screw fixation
articles.outcomes: Screw placement accuracy, guide-wire adjustments, fluoroscopy frequency, insertion time, operative time, blood loss, fracture reduction quality, hip function, and complications
articles.take_home: Robotic navigation-assisted placement of infra-acetabular screws was more accurate and efficient than conventional freehand placement, with 96% of screws placed perfectly in the robotic group compared to 60% in the freehand group, whilst achieving similar long-term hip function and safety outcomes.

articles.title: The prevalence of mental health service use after long-term minor-to-moderate motor vehicle crash injury: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Yu S, Griffiths D, Armfield N, Gray S, Di Donato M, Collie A
articles.population: Australians with work-related minor to moderate motor vehicle crash injuries and workers' compensation claims lasting over 24 months
articles.outcomes: Mental health service use within 24 months post-injury; determinants of service use including sex and prior mental health service history
articles.take_home: People with minor to moderate motor vehicle crash injuries used mental health services much more often than the general population, with about one in three using services within two years. Women and those who had used mental health services before their injury were more likely to use them afterwards.

articles.title: Is surgeon technique a modifiable risk factor for heterotopic ossification after posterior acetabular fracture fixation? A multi-surgeon study.
articles.authors: Kumar DS, Luther L, Schaffer NE, Litten RM, Traven SA, Moore RS, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing acetabular fracture fixation through posterior approach without HO prophylaxis
articles.sample_size: 1292 patients treated by 14 orthopaedic surgeons at two Level 1 trauma centres
articles.outcomes: Heterotopic ossification graded as little-to-no (grade 0-I), moderate (grade II), or severe (grade III-IV) using Brooker classification
articles.take_home: Severe heterotopic ossification after posterior acetabular fracture surgery is mainly determined by patient and injury factors such as severe head injury and mechanical ventilation, not by surgeon technique. Aggressive debridement of muscle and other technical factors do not meaningfully reduce the risk of severe ossification.

articles.title: Influencing factors of the long-term predictive accuracy of the ocular trauma score.
articles.authors: Li W, Fan N, Mei Z, Liu R, Peng Q
articles.population: Patients with mechanical eye trauma
articles.outcomes: Best-corrected visual acuity at median 14 months follow-up and accuracy of the Ocular Trauma Score in predicting vision outcomes
articles.take_home: The Ocular Trauma Score is useful for predicting eye injury outcomes but tends to be too pessimistic in severe injuries, underestimating how well some patients recover. Certain factors like infection or penetrating injuries were linked to better vision recovery than the score predicted.

articles.title: Orthopaedic Care in Brazil: Universal Coverage, Unequal Access, and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Giordano V, Kojima K, Pires RE, Labronici PJ, Belangero WD
articles.population: Brazil's population of over 200 million people
articles.outcomes: Availability and access to orthopaedic care; trauma case management; rehabilitation barriers
articles.take_home: Brazil has universal health coverage and strong orthopaedic training, but orthopaedic care is unevenly distributed, with major cities well served whilst rural and interior regions have poor access. High-volume trauma centres handle complex cases but face challenges with rehabilitation.

articles.title: Association of tranexamic acid with early death or massive transfusion after severe pelvic ring fractures: A nationwide registry-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Matsumoto S, Aoki M, Shimizu M
articles.population: Adults with severe pelvic ring fractures (Abbreviated Injury Scale severity 3 or higher)
articles.outcomes: Death within 24 hours after arrival or massive transfusion (at least 20 red blood cell units within 24 hours after injury)
articles.take_home: Patients who received tranexamic acid for severe pelvic fractures had lower rates of early death or massive transfusion compared to those who did not, but this association weakened when accounting for timing of treatment and was not accompanied by reduced transfusion requirements overall. The study cannot confirm a definite survival benefit from tranexamic acid for pelvic fractures.

articles.title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Yoon YC, Song HK
articles.population: Adults with severe pelvic ring injuries who were hemodynamically unstable and survived at least 24 hours
articles.sample_size: 98 patients (49 treated with REBOA, 49 non-REBOA controls); 75 survived to hospital discharge
articles.outcomes: Functional status at long-term follow-up (median 19 months), deep surgical site infection after pelvic fixation, and nonunion rates
articles.take_home: Patients who survived severe pelvic injuries after REBOA treatment had worse long-term functional recovery and much higher rates of deep infection and bone nonunion compared to those not treated with REBOA. The study cannot confirm REBOA directly caused these problems, but identifies this group as higher-risk for complications.

articles.title: Impact of sarcopenic obesity phenotype on long-term survival in geriatric trauma: A nationwide cohort study using weight-adjusted waist index.
articles.authors: Kim HG, Ju UC, Kim JY, Jung E
articles.population: Elderly patients aged 65 and over who experienced heavy trauma requiring hospitalisation, surgery, or ICU admission
articles.outcomes: 20-year mortality, hip and femur fractures, ICU stay duration
articles.take_home: Elderly trauma patients with high Weight-Adjusted Waist Index (a measure of muscle loss combined with excess fat) had significantly higher mortality risk over 20 years compared to those with low indices, particularly those who were obese or inactive. This measurement was better at predicting survival than BMI alone.

articles.title: Osteoporosis treatment gaps and risk of recurrent hip fracture following initial fragility fracture: Insights from over one million cases.
articles.authors: Laurore C, Lezak BA, Xie J, Avila A, Hong C, Yassin S, et al.
articles.population: Adults who had surgery for a first hip fracture
articles.outcomes: Risk of a second hip fracture within 1, 2 and 5 years
articles.take_home: Patients who started bone-health medication within six months of their first hip fracture were much less likely to have a second hip fracture compared to those who received no medication. Even patients already taking medication at the time of fracture had lower risk of recurrence.

articles.title: Articular compliance and tolerance to residual incongruity after intra-articular fracture: A hypothesis-driven narrative review.
articles.authors: Dhar SA, Dar TA, Dar RA, Farooq S, Maajid A, Zargar S, et al.
articles.population: Intra-articular fractures across multiple joint types
articles.outcomes: Tolerance of residual articular incongruity and risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis
articles.take_home: The thickness and stiffness of cartilage and bone beneath it may explain why different joints tolerate misalignment differently, but current evidence does not prove this. The authors propose measuring incongruity relative to cartilage thickness rather than in millimetres alone, and suggest further research to test this idea.

articles.title: The association of ABO Rh blood groups with 30-day mortality following traumatic injury - A retrospective observational study in the East of England.
articles.authors: Li J, Bell R, Basheer B, Boyle A, Barnard E, Bowman J, et al.
articles.population: Trauma patients aged 16 years and over admitted to East of England Major Trauma Centre
articles.outcomes: 30-day all-cause mortality across ABO RhD blood groups
articles.take_home: Patients with O negative blood group had a higher 30-day death rate after traumatic injury (15.1%) compared to other blood groups (8.8%). The reasons for this association are not yet understood.

articles.title: Lumbopelvic fixation for high-energy sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of complications, unplanned revision and implant removal.
articles.authors: Patel HA, Patel S, Suresh RI, Yang E, Lindley AK, Kidd G, et al.
articles.population: Patients with high-energy sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation treated with lumbopelvic fixation
articles.sample_size: 25 studies included; 564 patients across 19 high-energy cohorts
articles.outcomes: Surgical-site infection, implant loosening or failure, nonunion, loss of reduction, unplanned revision, implant removal, blood loss and operative time
articles.take_home: After lumbopelvic fixation for serious sacral fractures, infection and wound problems are the main reasons patients need further surgery, occurring in about 1 in 8 cases. Bone healing problems are uncommon, though whether to remove the metal work afterwards depends on each hospital's policy rather than medical need.

articles.title: Fracture characteristics in coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus: Clinical significance of medial trochlear involvement.
articles.authors: Ishihara N, Saeki M, Fujihara Y, Saeki S, Tanaka H, Ota H, et al.
articles.population: Patients with surgically treated coronal shear fractures of the distal humerus
articles.sample_size: 35 coronal shear fractures from 374 surgically treated distal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Elbow range of motion (flexion, extension, arc of motion) and bone-related complications at minimum 12 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Coronal shear fractures of the humerus involving the medial trochlea (a part of the elbow joint) were associated with greater loss of elbow extension and more complications such as non-union or infection compared to fractures without this involvement. Imaging to detect this type of fracture pattern may help surgeons plan better treatment.

articles.title: Global research on cricket injuries (1982-2025): A bibliometric analysis.
articles.authors: Vaishya R, Singh A, Gupta BM, Vaish A, Dhillon MS, Parmar Y, et al.
articles.population: Global cricket injury research publications from 1982 to 2025
articles.sample_size: Top 100 cited papers and top 10 highly cited papers examined in detail
articles.outcomes: Research growth trends, publication productivity by country and institution, citation impact, collaboration networks, and major research themes in cricket injuries
articles.take_home: Cricket injury research has grown significantly in the past two decades, with studies showing that fast bowlers have the highest injury rates, particularly to the lower back and legs. Monitoring training workload and understanding how bowlers' technique affects their spine appear to be key areas for preventing injuries.

articles.title: Hollow viscus injury (HVI) score in adult patients sustaining non-motor vehicle collision blunt trauma: A single-center retrospective validation study.
articles.authors: Nguyen PD, Grigorian A, Dieu AL, Nie J, Finney N, Kuza CM, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients aged over 18 years with non-motor vehicle collision blunt abdominal trauma who underwent CT imaging
articles.sample_size: 752 patients, 19 with confirmed hollow viscus injury
articles.outcomes: The HVI Score achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.96, with 100% sensitivity and 100% negative predictive value at the low-risk threshold, and 99% specificity and 47% positive predictive value at the high-risk threshold
articles.take_home: A prediction score originally developed for motor vehicle collision patients works very well at identifying hollow viscus injury in people with other types of blunt abdominal trauma. The score could help clinicians decide which patients need surgery and which can be safely observed.

articles.title: Comparative trends of musculoskeletal injury in pickleball and tennis: An 11-year analysis of U.S. emergency department visits.
articles.authors: Kiehl D, Ibrado R, Axelrod A, Vincent HK
articles.population: Patients presenting to US emergency departments with pickleball or tennis injuries
articles.sample_size: 4141 cases (1442 pickleball, 2699 tennis); national estimates of 80,553 pickleball and 110,480 tennis injuries
articles.outcomes: Anatomical location of injury, diagnosis type, injury mechanism, hospital admission rates, and annual trends in ED visits from 2014 to 2024
articles.take_home: Pickleball injuries to emergency departments are increasing over time, particularly among older adults aged 65 and over. Pickleball injuries involve more fractures and wrist injuries than tennis, which more commonly causes ankle sprains and strains, and pickleball players require hospital admission more often.

articles.title: Machine learning models with SHAP explanations for predicting neurosurgical intervention and six month functional outcome after traumatic brain injury.
articles.authors: Zhou Z, Cheng H, Liu H, Zhang D, Wang Q, Shao X
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using machine learning
articles.population: Adults with traumatic brain injury evaluated at a single centre
articles.sample_size: 673 patients (75 with unfavourable outcomes, 66 requiring surgery)
articles.outcomes: Need for neurosurgical intervention and six-month functional outcome (favourable versus unfavourable)
articles.take_home: Computer models using admission information like Glasgow Coma Scale, pupil responses and blood tests could predict whether patients would need brain surgery and their function at six months with reasonable accuracy, but the findings need to be tested independently before doctors could use them in practice.

articles.title: Geography matters: Variations in neck trauma between urban and rural level-II trauma centers.
articles.authors: Goldstein AL, Nino E, Biton D, Kruyer VN, Bar-Haim R, Laks S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with neck trauma treated at level-II trauma centres
articles.outcomes: Injury patterns, ICU admission rates, ICU length of stay, transfers to level-I centres, operative interventions, airway procedures, and CT angiography use
articles.take_home: Rural trauma centres see more severe blunt neck injuries from transport accidents and transfer patients to higher-level care, whilst urban centres treat more localised penetrating injuries with surgery. This suggests that trauma protocols should be tailored to match the different types of injuries each centre is likely to encounter.

articles.title: Limb preservation and optimization: A whole-patient approach to comprehensive care after catastrophic extremity injuries.
articles.authors: Cook JL, Rucinski K, Nuelle JAV, Royse LA, London DA, Lalonde SP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study using registry data
articles.population: Patients with catastrophic extremity injuries treated at a Limb Preservation and Optimization Center
articles.outcomes: Limb amputation rate (17.9%), return to work rates (71.6% at full capacity among those who returned), reoperation rates by injury type, treatment failure rates (11% to 100% depending on injury category)
articles.take_home: Most patients with severe limb injuries can be treated without amputation, though they typically need multiple operations. About 75-88% of patients returned to some form of work, with bone and fracture injuries having better outcomes than other injury types.

articles.title: Epidemiological characteristics and comparison of clinical outcomes between conservative and surgical treatment for rib fractures in South China: A 10‑year retrospective cohort study of 4085 cases with propensity score‑matching analysis.
articles.authors: Zhang T, Cai Q, Liang B, Song X
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Hospitalised patients with rib fractures in South China
articles.sample_size: 4085 patients overall; 723 patients (586 conservative, 137 surgical) in treatment comparison
articles.outcomes: Hospital stay, total costs, injury mechanisms, complications, epidemiological characteristics
articles.take_home: Patients treated conservatively for rib fractures had shorter hospital stays (3 days versus 17 days) and lower costs (5879 RMB versus 69,588 RMB) compared to surgery. Treatment choice should depend on injury type and severity, as surgical patients typically had more severe injuries like combined air and fluid in the lungs.

articles.title: Does greater orthoplastic integration reduce deep infection after open tibial fracture? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Choi B, Ghaie S, Shah A, Boriani F
articles.population: Patients with open tibial fractures
articles.outcomes: Deep infection rates, non-union rates, limb salvage rates, and reoperation rates across four models of orthoplastic integration
articles.take_home: Closer working between orthopaedic and plastic surgeons reduces deep infection risk after open leg fractures, with infection rates falling from 37% when surgeons work separately to 8% when they operate together in the same setting. Better integrated care also reduced non-union rates, though limb salvage was high across all models.

articles.title: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries: A 13-year retrospective review of injury characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.
articles.authors: Ibrahimov J, Bagir M, Bolat I, Kocaer O, Bozkurt O
articles.population: Paediatric patients with flexor tendon lacerations
articles.outcomes: Total Active Motion, Strickland score, grip and pinch strength, sensation, and QuickDASH questionnaire at mean follow-up of 59.9 months
articles.take_home: Most children (81-89%) had good or excellent results after surgery for flexor tendon injuries, with low complication rates. Younger children (0-5 years) did slightly less well than older children (6-12 years), and injuries with nerve damage had poorer outcomes.

articles.title: Gabapentinoid-opioid co-prescription after long bone fracture fixation is associated with increased 1-year nonunion.
articles.authors: Mahatme RJ, Moore SA, Gangavaram A, Moon E, Khadilkar S, Woolnough T, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study using propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults undergoing surgery for closed long bone fractures (tibia, humerus, or femur) who were opioid-naive and gabapentinoid-naive
articles.sample_size: Approximately 2000 patients per cohort after matching (range 1946-2012)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: prolonged opioid use (30-90 days) and chronic opioid use (90-180 days). Secondary outcomes: 30-day emergency department visits, 30-day readmissions, 1-year nonunion, and 1-year reoperation.
articles.take_home: Patients who received both gabapentinoids and opioids after fracture surgery had higher rates of bone nonunion and reoperation at one year compared to those receiving opioids alone, despite having fewer emergency department visits in the first month. The study suggests that while this combination may help with short-term pain relief, it may be associated with worse healing outcomes.
